sentences.text: Alexandronectes was a long-necked marine reptile belonging to the elasmosaurid plesiosaur family, containing only one known species, A. zealandiensis.
This animal differs from other aristonectines by having a smaller skull, distinct paroccipital processes, and a different mandibular glenoid.
Fossils of Alexandronectes were discovered by Alexander McKay in the Conway Formation of Canterbury.
The holotype specimens, cataloged as M Zfr 73 and CM Zfr 91, were formally described in 2016 by Otero et al. in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
Researchers classified Alexandronectes within the Elasmosauridae family and the Aristonectinae subfamily based on its pterygoid structure and an A-shaped squamosal arch.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Kaiwhekea is the closest relative of Alexandronectes.
While the Conway Formation fossils date to the Early Maastrichtian stage, the fossil range of Alexandronectes also includes the Campanian stage.
